key_steps: 1) OCBV-2 += ontosage:AccessPolicy {appliesToRole, scopeSpaces, scopeModalities, minAggregationSensors(k), resolutionTier[recency->maxResolutionSeconds], rateLimit[count,window], inferenceClass(individual_presence=deny)}. 2) config/access_policy_template.yaml -> scripts/generate_access_policies.py -> <id>_policies.ttl (defaults mirror BuildingChat tiers: own-space unrestricted; public 1-sensor; cross-space k>=14 across >=7 spaces; 15min->5s, 1h->1min, 1wk->1h). 3) Validator + zero-literal scan.
acceptance_criteria: Policies upload as triples for the active building; a SPARQL query lists a role's permissions; scans green.
verify: TTL validator; live SPARQL probe listing policies per role.
notes: VERIFICATION NOTE (plan review 2026-08-15): the default policy template MUST include a full-access benchmark/researcher role mapped to the replay user, so every pre-PROTECT baseline stays comparable after enforcement lands. Without it, T39 would silently change the meaning of all earlier replay/L7 numbers (clamped data = different answers) and the V4-vs-V5 delta becomes unmeasurable. || USER REQUIREMENT (2026-08-15): generator must support --profile standard|demo_open. demo_open = every role gets analyst-grade full READ (demo: anyone asks anything); DB writes remain impossible from chat regardless (no write path; admin endpoints need system:admin). Recommendation pending user choice: keep individual-presence denials even in demo_open (honest declines demo well). CLARIFIED vs existing layers: role_datasource_access.yaml stays as coarse source gate (keyword-routing enforcement, shallow); PROTECT adds query-parameter dimension at fetch chokepoints. || DONE 2026-08-15: scripts/generate_access_policies.py (profiles standard|demo_open; --all emits <id>_policies.ttl into input/ + bldg1/ + bldg3/; identity+namespace read from each building.yaml — zero literals, scan-listed). 12 policy instances per building (3 wildcard inference-class denials + 9 role policies). bldg2 UPLOADED (sha bdeb99ce) and VERIFIED via live SPARQL role listing (acceptance met). DEMO SWITCH for later: rerun with --profile demo_open --all then restart orchestrator (inference denials remain active by user decision). Parked buildings upload their TTLs automatically on their next activation.

title: Policy Decision Point (deterministic PDP service)
objective: One deterministic evaluator for every lane: (role x spaces x modalities x window x resolution x sensor-count x rate) -> allow | restrict(clamps) | deny(reason + nearest-allowed alternative). No LLM in the decision.
key_steps: 1) services/privacy/policy_engine.py: loads policy triples per building (cached, invalidated on TTL upload); pure-function verdicts. 2) Rate accounting in Redis (per user, sliding window). 3) Verdict carries policy id + parameters for provenance. 4) Unit tests incl. tier boundaries, k-floors, rate exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: PDP passes a table-driven matrix (>=30 cases); verdicts deterministic and building-agnostic.
notes: DONE 2026-08-18. services/privacy/policy_engine.py — PolicyEngine loads the building's ontosage:AccessPolicy triples (12 on bldg2; injected sparql_exec; reload() after TTL uploads; set_policies() for tests), evaluate() is PURE: order = inference-class denials (bind EVERY role incl. admin, per user decision #2) -> SCOPE-AWARE role policy (exact scope, then 'any'; DEFAULT scope='any' = the conservative cross-space policy — live shakedown caught the occupant 3-policy model own/public/any where first-match wrongly picked unrestricted 'own') -> rate limit (sliding window per user, injectable store, clock injectable) -> k-anonymity floors -> resolution tiers by data age (recency_min:max_res_s, '0:1'=unrestricted, beyond last tier=coarsest). Verdict carries policy IRI + parameters (privacy provenance for T39 dossiers), RESTRICT carries clamps (resolution_s, min_sensors/spaces), every DENY carries a nearest-allowed alternative. Tests: tests/test_policy_engine.py 37 (32-case matrix incl. tier boundaries, k-floors, scope fallbacks, rate exhaustion+slide+per-user isolation, determinism, provenance). LIVE bldg2 (12 real policies): admin+individual_presence DENY; occupant 3-sensor default-scope RESTRICT >=14/>=7; fm 30min/5s RESTRICT clamp 60s; admin raw ALLOW; unknown role DENY; same-verdict-across-restart TRUE. Suite 1298 pass/4 skip.

title: Enforcement by construction: adapters + ARBITER admission + reflex lanes
objective: PDP verdicts enforced where data is FETCHED so no lane can bypass; ARBITER declares restrictions as assumptions and cites the policy in the dossier (privacy provenance).
key_steps: 1) Fetch chokepoints (sql lane, deliberation fetch, event adapter later) consult PDP; restrict-clamps applied (resolution via aggregation, k-floor via min-sensor grouping); deny -> structured refusal upstream. 2) Admission gate gains 4th outcome 'restrict' -> proceed with declared assumption ('aggregated to 1h per policy P-xx'). 3) Dossier += applied_policies[]. 4) Role sourced from RBAC session only (personas stay non-authoritative).
acceptance_criteria: Restricted query returns clamped data WITH policy cited in dossier; denied query never touches the DB (adapter call logs prove zero fetches); all lanes covered.
verify: Integration tests + live probes incl. adapter-log assertion on deny.
notes: DONE 2026-08-18 (shadow phase live; enforce=on proven by test, flip is a config change). services/privacy/enforcement.py: consult() at the fetch chokepoints — SQL lane (_sql_node BEFORE fetch_data_for_uuids), deliberate node (verdict -> dossier applied_policies), events node (shadow log). PROTECT_ENFORCE setting: off|shadow(default)|on. Role from RBAC session ONLY (user_role; personas never). K-FLOOR SCOPING DECISION: min-sensor/space floors forwarded only for PRESENCE-ADJACENT modalities (occupancy/door/window/access/presence) — temperature over 1 sensor identifies nobody and would have blocked every basic occupant question; tier clamps still apply to everything. Verdict provenance: dossier gained applied_policies (render '**Privacy:** computed under access policy — ...', numeric_guard covers it); refusal_payload carries policy id + nearest-allowed alternative + zero rows. PDP singleton warm-load in lifespan (+150s); policy reload hooked into admin TTL upload when body contains 'AccessPolicy'. Tests: test_protect_enforcement.py 9 — incl. THE INVARIANT: enforce=on + deny -> _sql_node returns refusal with ZERO sql_agent calls (RecordingSQLAgent); shadow -> exactly 1 call, unchanged. LIVE bldg2 shadow: '[protect] lane=sql mode=shadow role=occupant modality=temperature n_sensors=1 -> ALLOW' + lane=events ALLOW; answers byte-normal (20.9C reading; 442 arrivals). replaytest's real role IS occupant. Suite 1307 pass/4 skip. REMAINING for enforce=on live flip (T42 gate): per-role test users + PROTECT_ENFORCE=on in .env + restart; rate store is per-process dict (Redis-backed store = T40).

title: Policy-denial reformulation (consent-based alternatives)
objective: Their best UX idea in our clarify machinery: a deny proposes the nearest ALLOWED reformulation as options; consent binds and resumes the parked plan.
key_steps: 1) clarify_policy += policy-slot asks (options computed by PDP: aggregate-up, coarsen-window, public-scope). 2) Same park/resume flow; no re-ask loops. 3) Decline text explains the policy in plain language from the policy triples' rdfs:comment.
acceptance_criteria: A denied deliberative query asks ONE consented alternative and resumes on choice; reflex denials explain + suggest without parking.
notes: DONE 2026-08-18. services/privacy/reformulation.py — a denial now proposes the nearest ALLOWED question, computed from the verdict's OWN parameters (never generic): RESTRICT -> aggregate-up to the actual k-floor (">=14 sensors / >=7 spaces"), coarsen to the actual tier ("5-second/1-hour average"), or ask a more recent window; DENY -> a room-level REWRITE of the person question ('Is the professor in her office?' -> 'Is anyone in that office right now? (a count, not an identity)'; badge history -> 'How many entries were recorded at that door today?'), plus aggregate + own-space options; rate-limit -> the retry window; missing policy -> ask an admin. explain() prefers the BUILDING'S OWN policy rdfs:comment so operators change wording by editing triples, not code. Wired into enforcement.refusal_payload (all fetch-chokepoint denials) and the privacy_refusal lane. Tests: test_policy_reformulation.py 9 + updated enforcement contract tests (now assert 'You can instead:' + options). NOTE vs the spec's park/resume idea: reformulations are OFFERED inline rather than parked as a clarify slot — a denial that parks a plan invites re-ask loops, and the user can simply ask the suggested question. Suite 1381 pass.

Reconstruction probe documented (BuildingChat's admitted untested limitation — we have a concrete trap + per-user PDP rate window; Redis store = T40). title: Admin portal policy editor (governance)
objective: Operationalize their declared open problem: policies authored via GUI into versioned TTL.
key_steps: 1) Admin tab: list/edit policy triples (role x scope x k x tiers x rate) with validation. 2) Writes <id>_policies.ttl via existing upload endpoint; audit note of who changed what. 3) Operator docs snippet.
acceptance_criteria: Admin edits a k-floor in GUI; next query reflects it (cache invalidation verified); change audit-logged.
notes: 2026-08-19 DONE - live-probed end to end, 3/3 on the acceptance criterion plus 10/11 on the API surface. Built: services/policy_admin.py (guided form -> validated Turtle, weakening diff, cache invalidation), input_ttl_store.upsert_policy/remove_policy writing input/<id>_policies.ttl, three admin endpoints under system:admin, a PoliciesTab in the portal, and an operator section in docs/SECURITY.md. TWO DELIBERATE REFUSALS, both verified live: a change that lowers a k floor or relaxes a limit is REJECTED unless acknowledge_weakening is set (the response naming each thing that got weaker), and an inference-class rule can be neither authored as anything but ':deny' nor deleted here. ACCEPTANCE: with the PDP enforced, an occupant asking 'How many people are in the building right now?' got 'about 298 people'; the governing policy's k floor was raised to 900/400 through the API; and the NEXT question was refused, quoting the policy's own comment - no restart, no stale cache. Getting there required fixing two P1s the probe exposed: BUG-194 (a policy edit was SHADOWED by a stale copy in the default graph - file and named graph correct, API and enforcement using the OLD value, editor reporting success throughout) and BUG-195 (the sparql lane could answer a reading question with no PDP chokepoint at all, AND 'how many people' was not recognised as presence-adjacent so the k-check was skipped even when the PDP ran). 27 unit tests for the editor + 16 for the modality inference.

title: Multi-model benchmark (accuracy AND invariance)
objective: Their 6-LLM accuracy table, answered with a stronger claim: guarantees that do not vary with the model.
key_steps: 1) Harness: generated L7 bank + flagship + policy-trap bank across >=4 models (gpt-oss:20b + >=2 more local via OLLAMA_MODEL + 1 OpenAI) - llm_manager makes this env-only. 2) Per model: behavior/proof/top1/FABRICATED/leak + latency + tokens. 3) Plan-fingerprint invariance across models (headline). 4) Paper table.
acceptance_criteria: Table complete for >=4 models; fabricated=0 and leak=0 on EVERY model; deliberative fingerprints identical.
notes: 2026-08-19. Harness + results in scripts/outputs/V5_T44_RESULTS.md. MODEL SLATE: probed all 19 hosted ids - only 7 reachable on this key (gpt-oss:120b/20b, gemma4:31b, minimax-m3, nemotron-3-nano/-super/-ultra); deepseek-v4-*/qwen3.5/glm-5.x/kimi-*/mistral-large-3 return HTTP 403 'requires a subscription' - excluded for ACCESS, not suitability; a paid plan is the one item blocked on the user. GUARANTEES THAT HOLD: 0 fabricated and 0 leaks on every complete arm and every repeat, hosted 120B and local 20B, PDP enforced (36 and 38 of 39 traps PASS, 0 wrongful denials). INVARIANCE - a correction of my own earlier claim: the probe was comparing plan_hash, which is sha256(plan_fingerprint | sorted candidate IRIs | fetch_window | basis) and therefore folds in live building state (the candidate set excludes currently-busy rooms), so it MUST differ between runs by design. cqir.plan_fingerprint(), documented in code as 'the determinism anchor', was never surfaced - it existed only inside plan_hash, so nobody could measure determinism even in principle (BUG-184). Now published in ExecutionOutcome, the dossier and plan_trace; harness compares it. RE-MEASURED on the right field: 5/8 identical (vs 3/8 on plan_hash), splitting into 2/8 lane downgrades (routing/admission, not compile) and 1/8 genuine compile divergence - i.e. 5/6 conditional on reaching the deliberative lane. The one divergence is semantic drift, not noise: 'find me a warm room' compiled to the SAME fingerprint as 'most comfortable place to sit'. A layered offline probe (host Ollama, temp 0, byte-identical prompt, 6 repeats) showed the provider does return different text at temp 0 but the parser absorbs nearly all of it (fingerprints 1/6, 1/6, 2/6 distinct). HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED: CAVEAT-182 (neither set nor recorded PROTECT_ENFORCE, so the first run's leak column measured shadow mode and read as a regression against T42's 0 leaks), no per-arm checkpointing, the repeat arm being scored as a model arm, and BUG-186 (a cp1252 console crash that killed run_all_graders before it ran a single grader). CAVEAT-185: deepseek-r1:32b spills the 16GB GPU into RAM and times out 8/8. CAVEAT-187: the Docker daemon wedged after ~30 recreates; user restarted, stack and all 4.6M triples intact. REMAINING: raise the same-model floor to 8/8 before any cross-model number; hosted arms need the quota window to reset.
